newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals rise, trade centres on PGM.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals rise, trade centres on PGM.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended higher on Tuesday, supported by the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Activity centred on the platinum group metals (PGM).
Palladium futures extended early gains to end higher after falling for three consecutive days.

"Caution that palladium has been oversold, stimulated active short-covering. Even if Japan-Russia PGM export contract talks start in early June, the first PGM shipments from Russia under new contracts are likely in July," a trader said.
Benchmark April ended nine yen per gram up at 571 yen.
The trader said palladium trade would continue to be volatile until Russian supplies start flowing into the market and alleviate the current tight situation.

"Short positions held by private investors in TOCOM palladium futures rose to about 59 tonnes as of Monday as they built fresh shorts in the past week. This may also exert upward pressure on prices," one commodity broker said.
Platinum futures were lifted by gains in spot platinum prices. Benchmark April platinum was up seven yen at 1,366 yen.
Gold futures moved in line with the currency market.
Investors were engaged in both buying and selling.

Activity in gold futures ebbed in late trade amid uncertainty over the near-term direction in the currency market. Gold futures ranged from three yen to 12 yen per gram higher. Benchmark April was up six yen at 1,278 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $342.70/343.00 per ounce at 0753 GMT, against $342.50/343.00 in late Tokyo trade on Monday.
"Activity in the bullion market was quiet following a holiday in overseas markets on Monday. Gold prices are expected to be range-bound on Tuesday," one trader said.
Benchmark April silver closed 0.4 yen per 10 grams higher at 179.2 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
